narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProductManufactured R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`MedicinalProductManufactured` is not present as an R6 resource. The R6 package marks the name as an old FHIR type and the apparent successor is `ManufacturedItemDefinition`. This is a hard resource-identity break for every direct R4 instance and a major code-generation/runtime break for clients, validators, REST endpoints, search parameter registries, and typed SDKs that still expect `resourceType: "MedicinalProductManufactured"`.

## Scope
I compared the R4 StructureDefinition with the likely R6 successor `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, using package indexes, type code systems, related local StructureDefinitions, and local ValueSet/CodeSystem files. I excluded inherited base-artifact changes from `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, and extension infrastructure.

## Main migration themes
The migration is not a simple rename. R6 adds a mandatory modifier `status`, removes the R4 mandatory root `quantity`, changes ingredient representation from references to R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` into coded/inbound `Ingredient` patterns, and remodels physical/other characteristics into a generic `property` list. R6 also adds optional definitional content such as identifiers, names, marketing status, and component hierarchies that cannot be represented cleanly in the R4 resource.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact issue is the root identity change: old instances are invalid in R6 without changing `resourceType` and canonical type references. The next highest risks are `status` becoming mandatory, the loss of direct `quantity`, and the ingredient/characteristic remodels, each of which requires policy-driven transformation rather than a mechanical field copy.

## Findings requiring human review
All material mappings require review because no official ConceptMap or narrative migration page was available locally. In particular, `quantity`, ingredients, and physical characteristics need domain-specific mapping rules to avoid losing medicinal-product meaning.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many changes appear to reflect a more mature R6 IDMP-style model, but several could have been less disruptive if the old resource name or old elements had been retained as deprecated aliases, optional compatibility elements, or cross-version extensions.

## Follow-up analysis
A complete migration plan should also assess R6 `Ingredient`, R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient`, R6 `PackagedProductDefinition`, and the relevant product terminology ValueSets with terminology expansion support.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductManufactured` has material breaking changes: the R4 resource is absent in R6 and is apparently replaced by `ManufacturedItemDefinition`. The top migration concerns are resource identity, mandatory R6 `status`, and non-mechanical remapping of `quantity`, ingredients, and physical characteristics. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official ConceptMap or narrative migration note.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a model transformation rather than a resource rename. Existing R4 data must change resource type and canonical references, assign an R6 lifecycle `status`, decide how to preserve the mandatory R4 `quantity`, translate ingredient references into R6 `Ingredient`/coded ingredient patterns, and remodel physical characteristics into R6 `property` entries. R6-to-R4 conversion is also lossy because R6 can carry identifiers, marketing status, components, and coded properties that the R4 resource did not support.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the assigned R6 resource name is absent and that `ManufacturedItemDefinition` is the likely successor, based on the R6 package index, `fhir-old-types`, `fhir-types`, and matching retained elements. Confidence is medium for precise migration recommendations because the local inputs do not include an official diff, ConceptMap, narrative migration page, or terminology expansions for the example bindings.

findings.title: R4 MedicinalProductManufactured resource is absent in R6 and appears renamed/replaced by ManufacturedItemDefinition

semanticText.definition: The manufactured item as contained in the packaged medicinal product.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 defines `MedicinalProductManufactured` as a concrete resource with `resourceType` value `MedicinalProductManufactured` and canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/MedicinalProductManufactured`.

newState.summary: No R6 StructureDefinition exists for MedicinalProductManufactured; the matching R6 resource is ManufacturedItemDefinition.

semanticText.definition: The definition and characteristics of a medicinal manufactured item, such as a tablet or capsule, as contained in a packaged medicinal product.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 does not include the assigned StructureDefinition name. The R6 old-types CodeSystem lists `MedicinalProductManufactured` as an old resource name, while `ManufacturedItemDefinition` is present as a concrete resource for the same manufactured-item concept.

facts.note: No `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductManufactured.json` is present in the R6 package.
R6 `CodeSystem-fhir-old-types` describes old resource names no longer used in this version.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `ManufacturedItemDefinition` is the only R6 StructureDefinition matching the manufactured-item name and semantics. It keeps the core concepts `manufacturedDoseForm`, `unitOfPresentation`, and `manufacturer`, and R6 uses it as a target from related medicinal-product resources.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct resource identity break. An R4 JSON/XML instance with `resourceType: "MedicinalProductManufactured"` is not an R6 `ManufacturedItemDefinition` instance and will not validate against the R6 resource set. Generated classes, switch statements, REST endpoint configuration, compartment/search registration, profile canonical URLs, and stored references that name the old resource must be updated. In the reverse direction, an R6 `ManufacturedItemDefinition` instance is not an R4 `MedicinalProductManufactured` resource without a cross-version transform.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The safety/business risk is primarily data interchange and regulatory traceability risk: manufactured-item records may be rejected or silently skipped if systems only recognize one resource identity.

justification.inferredGoal: Align the medicinal product model around a more explicit definitional resource name for manufactured items.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the old resource identity and canonical URL while updating title, aliases, definitions, and model content for the manufactured-item definition concept.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of a clearer R6 definitional manufactured-item model is reasonable, but a resource-type and canonical rename is one of the most disruptive ways to achieve it. The local evidence shows continuity of the business concept rather than a need for two incompatible identities. Because R6 could have kept `MedicinalProductManufactured` as the base resource identity and improved its title, definition, aliases, maturity, and element model, the identity break looks probably avoidable. Migration tooling or a ConceptMap would help implementers, but those are mitigations and are not counted here as the backward-compatible base design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have retained `resourceType: "MedicinalProductManufactured"` and the old StructureDefinition canonical while making the R6 definitional semantics explicit through metadata, definitions, and aliases such as "ManufacturedItemDefinition". That would preserve existing parsers, references, package allow-lists, and profile links for the resource identity. The tradeoff is living with a less consistent old name in the R6 resource inventory; if R6 also introduced `ManufacturedItemDefinition` as a separate resource for the same fact, duplicate representations could persist indefinitely, so simple retention of the old name is the cleaner compatibility alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves resource-type compatibility with moderate naming-consistency cost; adding a parallel new resource would risk duplicate same-concept representations.

evidence.detail: R4 defines a concrete resource with id/type `MedicinalProductManufactured`.
R6 defines `ManufacturedItemDefinition` for the manufactured-item concept.
The R6 package index contains `StructureDefinition-ManufacturedItemDefinition.json` and no `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductManufactured.json` entry.
R6 lists `MedicinalProductManufactured` as an old FHIR type no longer used in this version.
evidence.quote: An old resource name no longer used in this version of FHIR (deleted or renamed).

examples.examplesMd: The R4 fragment illustrates the resource-type identity break. It is intentionally minimal and focuses on the local mandatory R4 fields.

findings.narrativeMd: The assigned resource name does not survive into R6. This affects every direct instance and every implementation surface that keys behavior by resource type or canonical StructureDefinition URL. Even if the business concept continues as `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, migration requires changing identifiers, validators, generated models, profiles, references, and API routing rather than simply accepting old instances under a new version.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `resourceType: "MedicinalProductManufactured"` is old-valid but new-invalid in R6 because R6 has no such resource StructureDefinition. Conversely, R6 `ManufacturedItemDefinition` is not an R4 resource type. Strict parsers and generated SDKs will fail before element-level validation unless a cross-version adapter rewrites the resource type and canonical references.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Implement an explicit resource-level transform from R4 `MedicinalProductManufactured` to R6 `ManufacturedItemDefinition`. Update references, profile URLs, search/indexing code, package allow-lists, serialization tests, and generated model names. Do not rely on accepting the old resource type in R6 unless a deliberate compatibility layer is added.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change may be justified by a clearer definitional model, but it could have been made less disruptive by keeping a deprecated alias or publishing a normative ConceptMap. Without such compatibility machinery, all consumers must coordinate on the new resource identity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The successor identification is strong but inferred from local package evidence; an official migration note would be useful.

findings.title: R6 successor adds mandatory modifier status with a required publication-status binding

oldState.summary: R4 MedicinalProductManufactured had no local lifecycle status element.
oldState.narrativeMd: There is no `MedicinalProductManufactured.status` element in R4, so existing instances do not carry a base-resource lifecycle state for this manufactured item.

newState.summary: R6 ManufacturedItemDefinition.status is mandatory, modifier, and code-bound to publication-status.

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

semanticText.definition: The status of this item. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.
semanticText.comment: Allows filtering of manufactured items that are appropriate for use versus not.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires each `ManufacturedItemDefinition` to state a lifecycle status, and the element is marked as a modifier because status changes whether the item should be treated as usable/current.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This is a new local root element on the R6 successor; there is no R4 local element with the same semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: After changing the resource type to the R6 successor, an otherwise migrated R4 instance will still fail R6 validation unless `status` is supplied. The modifier flag raises runtime risk because applications must not ignore the value: `retired`, `draft`, `active`, and `unknown` affect whether the item is appropriate for use. R6-to-R4 conversion loses this lifecycle signal unless stored in an extension or external metadata.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Choosing an incorrect lifecycle status can cause retired or draft manufactured-item definitions to be treated as active, or active records to be filtered out.

justification.inferredGoal: Make manufactured item definitions lifecycle-manageable and filterable in the R6 definitional model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `status` optional in the base resource, or require it only in profiles and implementation guides.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding lifecycle status to a definitional manufactured-item resource is a reasonable R6 goal, and making it mandatory has concrete interoperability value because consumers can consistently filter draft, active, retired, and unknown definitions. A less-breaking design exists, but it materially weakens that goal: optional or profile-only status would leave many base R6 instances without a lifecycle signal and could lead to unsafe local defaults during migration. On balance, the break is probably justified, provided migrations do not blindly default every historical item to `active`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would define `ManufacturedItemDefinition.status` as `0..1` with the same required value set when present, then let regulatory profiles or best-practice invariants require it. That would allow R4-derived instances to validate without inventing a status. The cost is substantial: mixed R6 ecosystems could not rely on base instances carrying lifecycle state, and applications would need profile-specific logic or local assumptions before deciding whether a definition is usable.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but loses the base guarantee that every R6 manufactured item can be lifecycle-filtered; profile-only requiredness fragments behavior.

evidence.detail: No local R4 element `MedicinalProductManufactured.status` exists.
R6 `status` has cardinality 1..1, type `code`, `isModifier=true`, and a required publication-status binding.
The required status code system contains `draft`, `active`, `retired`, and `unknown`.

examples.examplesMd: The old-valid/new-invalid example is shown after the resource-type rewrite to isolate the missing R6 `status` validation failure. `unknown` is only appropriate when the migration policy cannot determine draft/active/retired; it should not be used as a generic catch-all for other statuses.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces a new required modifier element, `ManufacturedItemDefinition.status`. This is not just an optional metadata addition: any R4 record promoted to the R6 successor needs a lifecycle decision. Systems that ignore modifier elements could misinterpret retired or draft product definitions as usable.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances have no corresponding field. After resource-level migration, they are R6-invalid until a required status code is supplied. R6 instances with status can be serialized back to R4 only by dropping the value or carrying it in an extension, because the R4 resource has no local lifecycle status element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a migration policy for status assignment. Prefer deriving `active`, `draft`, or `retired` from authoritative regulatory/product lifecycle data; use `unknown` only when the source truly cannot determine the state. Add tests for omitted status, invalid status codes, and each valid lifecycle state.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The status requirement is understandable for a mature definitional resource, but it is disruptive because R4 did not collect this value. A profile-level requirement or optional base element would have allowed old data to remain valid while encouraging richer lifecycle management.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed to decide status defaults for historical data; automatically setting all records to `active` would be unsafe.

findings.title: Mandatory R4 quantity has no direct R6 successor element

oldState.summary: R4 required a 1..1 Quantity named quantity.

semanticText.short: The quantity or "count number" of the manufactured item
semanticText.definition: The quantity or "count number" of the manufactured item.

oldState.narrativeMd: Every valid R4 `MedicinalProductManufactured` instance must include `quantity`, representing the quantity or count number of the manufactured item.

newState.summary: R6 ManufacturedItemDefinition has no root quantity element; only more specific component/constituent amount fields exist.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 does not define `ManufacturedItemDefinition.quantity`. It has `component.amount` and `component.constituent.amount`, but those describe amounts of components or constituents rather than the old root item count.

facts.note: Related but not equivalent to the R4 root quantity/count field.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: No R6 root element has the R4 quantity name or definition. The R6 `amount` fields are nested under components/constituents and have different semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any direct field-copy migration that keeps `quantity` under the R6 successor will produce an unknown R6 element. Dropping it can lose data because R4 made the value mandatory. In the reverse direction, a valid R6 `ManufacturedItemDefinition` can omit any root item count, so an R4-conformant instance cannot be generated without inventing a mandatory `quantity` or using profile-specific assumptions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing or inventing item quantity/count can affect packaging, labeling, strength interpretation, and regulatory traceability.

justification.inferredGoal: Move away from a single root count toward a richer component/constituent representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated optional root `quantity` on the R6 successor while adding the richer component and constituent amount model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving toward a richer component/constituent representation may be a reasonable R6 goal, but the local definitions do not show a direct replacement for the mandatory R4 root `quantity`. Because every valid R4 instance had this value, dropping it creates avoidable validation and data-loss pressure. A base R6 compatibility field could preserve the old count while newer structures mature, so the level of breakage is not clearly justified by the available evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `ManufacturedItemDefinition.quantity` as a deprecated `0..1 Quantity` compatibility element, with definitions explaining when it represents the legacy manufactured-item count and how it relates to `component.amount`, `component.constituent.amount`, or packaging structures. This is a real base-design alternative, unlike an extension or conversion script. Its tradeoff is semantic overlap: implementations would need precedence and consistency rules, and deprecated quantity representations could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old mandatory data with moderate ambiguity risk around whether root quantity overlaps component, constituent, or packaging quantities.

evidence.detail: R4 `quantity` is 1..1 Quantity and summary=true.
No `ManufacturedItemDefinition.quantity` element exists in R6.
R6 component/constituent amount fields exist but are nested and describe component or constituent quantities, not the old root count.

examples.examplesMd: The first example isolates the R6 unknown-element problem after resource-type migration. The second shows an R6-valid shape with no root item count, which cannot satisfy R4's mandatory `quantity` without an external rule.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 treated the manufactured-item quantity/count as mandatory. R6 removes the direct field from the likely successor. This is both a validation problem for old payloads and a semantic migration problem because the old value may be important and has no obvious single destination in the R6 content model.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 payload retaining `quantity` under the R6 resource is new-invalid because the element is unknown. A valid R6 payload with no item count is not R4-representable without fabricating the R4 mandatory `quantity`. Component amount fields cannot be used blindly because they refer to component or constituent amounts rather than the old root item count.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory how source systems used R4 `quantity`. If it represented a package count or presentation count, preserve it through a documented extension, profile-specific mapping, or a related packaging structure rather than dropping it. Only map to `component.amount` or `component.constituent.amount` when domain review confirms the semantics are equivalent. Add round-trip tests for common counts, missing source quantities, and multi-component items.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 model may have intentionally moved quantity semantics into richer structures, but removing a mandatory field without a direct replacement is highly disruptive. A deprecated optional element or official extension would have preserved backward compatibility while allowing newer modeling patterns.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This is the highest element-level semantic uncertainty. Official narrative guidance would materially improve confidence.

findings.title: Ingredient changed from references to R4 MedicinalProductIngredient into coded/inbound R6 Ingredient patterns

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represents manufactured item ingredients as references to separate `MedicinalProductIngredient` resources.

newState.summary: R6 root ingredient is 0..* CodeableConcept; full ingredient resources link back through Ingredient.for, and component constituents can reference Ingredient using CodeableReference.

binding.description: This value set includes all substance codes from SNOMED CT - provided as an exemplar value set.

semanticText.short: The ingredients of this manufactured item. Only needed if these are not specified by incoming references from the Ingredient resource
semanticText.definition: The ingredients of this manufactured item. This is only needed if the ingredients are not specified by incoming references from the Ingredient resource.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `ManufacturedItemDefinition.ingredient` is a coded summary. Detailed ingredients are modeled as R6 `Ingredient` resources whose `for` references can target `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, or as component constituents with `hasIngredient` CodeableReference.

facts.note: Detailed ingredient resource linkage is reversed/inbound rather than a simple root reference list.
Nested component constituent linkage may represent some but not all old root ingredient references.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new paths share the name `ingredient`, but their type and usage changed substantially. The R6 definition explicitly says the root coded ingredients are only needed when incoming `Ingredient` references do not specify them.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 `ingredient.reference` object is not valid where R6 expects a `CodeableConcept`. Migration must either create/update R6 `Ingredient` resources that point back to the manufactured item, use coded summary ingredients, or model component constituents. Reverse conversion is also lossy: a coded R6 ingredient may not identify a full R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` resource, and inbound R6 `Ingredient.for` relationships are not contained in the manufactured item itself.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect ingredient migration can change product composition, strengths, allergen/excipient interpretation, or regulatory ingredient traceability.

justification.inferredGoal: Support both coded ingredient summaries and a separate R6 Ingredient resource model linked to products.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a root `CodeableReference` or retain a deprecated root ingredient reference alongside the coded summary and inbound `Ingredient.for` pattern.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears to be a cleaner ingredient model: root coded summaries are available when detailed `Ingredient` resources do not point back to the manufactured item, while full ingredient details live in a dedicated graph. That goal is reasonable and the old outward reference list is not obviously equivalent to the new model. A less-breaking design exists for common cases, but it would blur the distinction between summary ingredients and authoritative ingredient resources and could produce conflicting representations of clinically important composition data. The break is therefore probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have made the root element a `CodeableReference(Ingredient)` or added an explicit deprecated root reference element while also allowing coded summaries. This would let many reference-shaped R4 payloads survive the element-type transition more easily. It is only a partial alternative because the referenced R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` resource has its own identity/model migration, and allowing both root references and inbound `Ingredient.for` links would require strict consistency rules to avoid duplicate or contradictory ingredient facts.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve common reference-shaped data but creates duplicate ingredient representations and graph-consistency risks across root codes, root references, and inbound Ingredient resources.

evidence.detail: R4 `ingredient` is Reference targeting `MedicinalProductIngredient`.
R6 `ingredient` is CodeableConcept with an example substance-codes binding.
R6 `Ingredient.for` can reference `ManufacturedItemDefinition`, showing that detailed ingredients may be represented by inbound references.
R6 component constituents can refer to `Ingredient` with CodeableReference.

examples.examplesMd: The R4-shaped `ingredient.reference` is invalid for the R6 root `ingredient`, which is a CodeableConcept. The coded R6 example cannot become an R4 reference without creating or finding a separate ingredient resource.

findings.narrativeMd: The ingredient element keeps a familiar name but changes representation. In R4 it was a reference list to ingredient resources. In R6 the root element is a coded ingredient summary, while detailed ingredient resources are linked from outside the manufactured item or from nested component constituents. This can surprise implementers because a same-named field is not type-compatible.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 `Reference` objects under `ingredient` are new-invalid in R6. R6 coded ingredients are not directly R4-representable as references. Graph-based R6 ingredient relationships also require looking outside the resource, so a resource-local transform alone can miss data.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not mechanically copy the old `ingredient` array. For each R4 ingredient reference, decide whether to create an R6 `Ingredient` resource with `Ingredient.for` pointing to the manufactured item, emit a coded `ManufacturedItemDefinition.ingredient`, or use component constituent modeling. Maintain reference identity and strength/substance details from the old ingredient resource in the separate Ingredient migration. Test products with active ingredients, excipients, multiple ingredients, and missing referenced resources.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 pattern is likely justified by a more expressive ingredient model, but replacing a reference field with a CodeableConcept is a hard compatibility break. A root `CodeableReference(Ingredient)` could have supported both codes and references with less disruption.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Coordinate this finding with the separate `MedicinalProductIngredient`/`Ingredient` analysis; that resource owns many details needed for safe migration.

findings.title: Physical and other characteristics are remodeled from typed R4 fields into generic R6 property entries

oldState.summary: R4 had physicalCharacteristics 0..1 ProdCharacteristic and otherCharacteristics 0..* CodeableConcept.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 separated a typed `ProdCharacteristic` backbone-like datatype for dimensions, color, imprint, image, and scoring from a separate repeated `otherCharacteristics` CodeableConcept list.

newState.summary: R6 uses property 0..* with mandatory property.type and value[x] choices.

slicing.description: No explicit slicing; repeated generic property entries are distinguished by `property.type`.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 defines `ManufacturedItemDefinition.property` as repeated general characteristics. Each property has `type` 1..1 CodeableConcept and optional `value[x]` choices: CodeableConcept, Quantity, Range, date, boolean, markdown, Attachment, or Reference(Binary).

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `property` definition is the closest local successor for general/physical characteristics, but no official mapping was available from specific R4 ProdCharacteristic fields to R6 property type codes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 payloads containing `physicalCharacteristics` or `otherCharacteristics` cannot be copied to the R6 successor because those element names are gone. Migration also changes code-generation shape from named typed fields to a polymorphic list, which can break client code and FHIRPath expressions. R6 properties may not map cleanly back to R4 named fields, especially when property type codes do not match a known R4 ProdCharacteristic slot or when R6 uses value types such as Range, date, boolean, markdown, or Binary reference.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Physical characteristics such as color, imprint, scoring, and dimensions can be clinically or regulatory relevant for product identification.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize product characteristics into coded properties with flexible value types.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated named `physicalCharacteristics` and `otherCharacteristics` compatibility fields while introducing the generic `property` backbone.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing product characteristics into coded `property` entries is a reasonable model-evolution goal because fixed named fields are hard to extend across regulatory and product-identification use cases. A less-breaking base design could preserve common R4 shapes, but the tradeoffs are material: the same color, imprint, image, dimension, or scoring fact could appear in both old named slots and new generic properties, and the deprecated representation might never disappear. That makes the breaking remodel probably justified, although the lack of official property-type mappings remains a migration risk.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would keep `physicalCharacteristics` and `otherCharacteristics` as deprecated compatibility elements, or define explicit base slices that accept the old named facts while mapping them into `property.type` and `value[x]`. This would preserve many R4 instances. It is only partial because it introduces same-resource duplication, validation ambiguity when old and new values disagree, and implementation burden for clients that must support both named fields and the generic property list.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old named fields but duplicates the same characteristics in named and coded generic forms, requiring precedence and consistency rules.

evidence.detail: R4 `physicalCharacteristics` is 0..1 `ProdCharacteristic`.
R4 `otherCharacteristics` is 0..* `CodeableConcept`.
R4 `ProdCharacteristic` contains named fields such as height, width, depth, weight, nominalVolume, externalDiameter, shape, color, imprint, image, and scoring.
R6 uses repeated `property` entries with mandatory `property.type` and `property.value[x]` choices.
R6 `property.type` has an example binding to SNOMED CT observable entity descendants; no expansion was available locally.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative, not normative. Real migrations should use controlled `property.type` coding and appropriate value types where available.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 replaces R4's named physical-characteristic structure and separate other-characteristics list with a generic characteristic list. This is a structural and semantic change: consumers that expected `physicalCharacteristics.color` or `physicalCharacteristics.image` must now interpret repeated properties and their type codes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 characteristic elements are new-invalid under the R6 resource. R6 property entries are only partially R4-representable because not every property type has a named R4 slot, and R6 allows value types not present in R4 `ProdCharacteristic`. Strict generated clients will need new collection and choice-type handling.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create a mapping table from each R4 `ProdCharacteristic` child and each `otherCharacteristics` code to an R6 `property.type` code and value type. Preserve unmapped values in extensions or flag them for manual review. Test dimensions, repeated colors/imprints, images, scoring, and arbitrary other characteristics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The generic property model is flexible and likely easier to extend, but the change could have been less disruptive with deprecated named aliases or official property-type mappings. Without them, implementers must create local conventions that may not interoperate.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology expansion and narrative examples would improve confidence in the exact property-type coding strategy.

findings.title: R6 successor adds optional identifier, name, marketing status, and component hierarchy not present in R4

oldState.summary: R4 MedicinalProductManufactured had no local identifier, name, marketingStatus, or component hierarchy.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 resource was comparatively small and did not provide local elements for manufactured-item identifiers, descriptive names, marketing status, or intrinsic physical components.

newState.summary: R6 ManufacturedItemDefinition adds optional identifier/name/marketingStatus and a nested component model.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds `identifier` 0..*, `name` 0..1, `marketingStatus` 0..*, and `component` 0..*. The component hierarchy includes component type/function/amount, constituents with amount/location/function/hasIngredient, component properties, and nested components.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are new local elements on the R6 successor with no R4 local paths in `MedicinalProductManufactured`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These additions do not make old R4 instances invalid by themselves because they are optional in R6. They do, however, create substantial reverse-conversion risk: R6 instances can contain identifiers, marketing availability, and component/constituent structure that the R4 resource has no place to carry except extensions or related resources. Generated R4 models and down-conversion pipelines will drop this data unless explicitly handled.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Marketing status and component composition can be important for regulatory availability, packaging, and product identification workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Enrich the manufactured item definition with identifiers, availability, and detailed physical-component composition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed because these R6 additions are optional and do not invalidate R4-derived instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added identifier, name, marketing status, and component hierarchy make the R6 manufactured-item definition more expressive without requiring old R4 instances to supply those elements. Under the calibration rules this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue, even though it is important for down-conversion and round-trip planning. The optional additions are therefore justified as ordinary model enrichment.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the new elements are optional, R4-to-R6 compatibility for this finding is already preserved at the base-design level. The hard problem is the reverse direction: R6 instances that use these fields cannot be represented cleanly in the R4 resource. Cross-version extensions, sidecar records, or ConceptMaps may reduce that R6-to-R4 loss, but those are mitigation strategies rather than less-breaking alternatives to an R4-to-R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The remaining issue is R6-to-R4 information loss; extensions or ConceptMaps can mitigate that but are not backward-compatible base-design alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `identifier` 0..* Identifier.
R6 adds `name` 0..1 string.
R6 adds `marketingStatus` 0..* MarketingStatus.
R6 adds a repeated component hierarchy with nested constituents, properties, and subcomponents.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment uses only optional additions plus mandatory R6 fields. R4 has no local fields for the identifier/name/component content shown.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 expands the successor resource into a richer definitional model. This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because the added elements are optional, but it is a real round-trip and down-conversion risk for systems that must send R6 data to R4 recipients or persist it in R4-shaped stores.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instances remain unaffected by these optional additions. Valid R6 instances that use them are not cleanly R4-representable. A strict R4 serializer would either reject the fields or drop them, and generated R4 classes have no corresponding properties.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 paths, decide which new fields are essential and preserve them through extensions, sidecar records, related resources, or implementation-guide-specific profiles. For R4-to-R6 paths, consider whether identifiers, names, marketing status, or components can be populated from source systems rather than left empty.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are a normal, mostly backward-compatible way to evolve a model. The main avoidable gap is lack of local down-conversion guidance; official cross-version extensions would reduce information loss for mixed-version ecosystems.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding is primarily an R6-to-R4 representability issue and should be triaged with actual exchange-direction requirements.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: For comparable retained concepts, `manufacturedDoseForm` remains 1..1, `unitOfPresentation` remains 0..1, and `manufacturer` remains 0..*. Material cardinality/presence changes are reported separately for resource identity, mandatory `status`, removed `quantity`, and added optional R6 content.

Retained `manufacturedDoseForm` and `unitOfPresentation` remain `CodeableConcept`, and `manufacturer` remains `Reference(Organization)`. Material type/content-model changes are reported for `ingredient` and characteristics/property.
The retained `manufacturer` reference target remains `Organization`. Ingredient reference-target changes are not counted here because they are a material finding.

No R4 required or extensible local binding on a retained element was found to be strengthened. R6 adds example bindings for several CodeableConcept elements, which are not hard validation breaks. The new required `status` binding is reported as part of the mandatory status finding.

No local non-base invariant was found on the R4 or R6 local manufactured-item elements. DomainResource and Element constraints such as `dom-*`, `ele-1`, and extension constraints are inherited/base-artifact concerns and excluded from findings.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value constraints were found on the local elements compared in this report.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were found on the compared local elements.

Comparable retained local elements remain summary elements. Summary behavior changes from added/removed/remodeled elements are covered by their findings rather than treated as standalone flag changes.
No local slicing definitions were found on the compared R4 resource or R6 successor. The R6 repeated `property` and `component` structures are not declared as sliced in the base StructureDefinition.

No standalone local primitive serialization rule changed for retained scalar elements. The major serialization impacts are the resource type rename and the new/replaced content models, especially `status`, `ingredient`, and `property.value[x]`, all covered in findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Successor artifact metadata is more mature: R4 draft/trial-use/FMM 0 to R6 active/normative/FMM 2
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: StructureDefinition maturity metadata does not by itself make instances invalid. It does, however, signal that the R6 successor is more mature and may be subject to stronger conformance expectations.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review governance and product-regulatory workflows that key off artifact maturity or standards status. This is a planning signal, not an instance-validation break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds example terminology bindings for several coded concepts
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The inspected bindings for manufactured dose form, unit of presentation, ingredient, and property type are `example` strength, so they do not require instances to use those value sets for base validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Although not hard-breaking, these bindings are useful for choosing interoperable codes during migration. Terminology expansion would improve mapping quality.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Retained elements have refined wording but stable cardinality and broad type
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `manufacturedDoseForm`, `unitOfPresentation`, and `manufacturer` keep the same cardinality and broad type/target as their R4 counterparts. Wording was refined, such as clarifying the manufactured-dose-form timing and manufacturer multiplicity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Use the R6 definitions when validating semantic equivalence, but no standalone validation break was identified for these retained concepts.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R4 `MedicinalProductManufactured.ingredient` referenced `MedicinalProductIngredient`, while R6 uses `Ingredient.for` and `CodeableReference(Ingredient)` patterns. Safe migration requires the separate Ingredient resource analysis.

The R4 resource definition describes manufactured items as contained in packaged medicinal products. R6 packaged-product containment/reference patterns may affect where removed `quantity` or item identity should migrate, but those relationships belong to the packaged-product artifact analysis.
Example bindings are not hard-breaking, but terminology expansion and mapping support are important for reliable characteristic and ingredient migration.
Inherited constraints and base serialization behavior were deliberately excluded from local findings under the assignment scope rule and should be handled by the base-artifact reports.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official local ConceptMap or migration guide was found for `MedicinalProductManufactured` to `ManufacturedItemDefinition`. The successor match is strong, but detailed element mappings for quantity, ingredients, and characteristics remain partly inferential.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official R4/R6 ConceptMap or HL7 migration page that names the successor resource and maps old element paths to R6 paths.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The local ValueSets used for R6 example bindings were inspected by compose only. Without terminology expansion, this report cannot assess code-by-code continuity for manufactured dose forms, units of presentation, product characteristics, or substances.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansions against the relevant R4 and R6 ValueSets and compare available codes and displays.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Narrative R6 specification pages, examples, and ballot change notes were not used. This limits confidence about intended semantic equivalence for `quantity`, `component`, and `property` modeling.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official R6 narrative resource page, examples, and ballot reconciliation notes for manufactured item definitions.
